3: Out of the mouth of each one there protruded The feet of a transgressor, and the legs Up to the calf, the rest within remained.
8: In all of them the soles were both on fire; Wherefore the joints so violently quivered, They would have snapped asunder withes and bands.
13: Even as the flame of unctuous things is wont To move upon the outer surface only, So likewise was it there from heel to point.
18: “Master, who is that one who writhes himself, More than his other comrades quivering,” I said, “and whom a redder flame is sucking?”
23: And he to me: “If thou wilt have me bear thee Down there along that bank which lowest lies, From him thou’lt know his errors and himself.”
29: And I: “What pleases thee, to me is pleasing; Thou art my Lord, and knowest that I depart not From thy desire, and knowest what is not spoken.”
35: Straightway upon the fourth dike we arrived; We turned, and on the left-hand side descended Down to the bottom full of holes and narrow.
40: And the good Master yet from off his haunch Deposed me not, till to the hole he brought me Of him who so lamented with his shanks.
45: “Whoe’er thou art, that standest upside down, O doleful soul, implanted like a stake,” To say began I, “if thou canst, speak out.”
50: I stood even as the friar who is confessing The false assassin, who, when he is fixed, Recalls him, so that death may be delayed.
55: And he cried out: “Dost thou stand there already, Dost thou stand there already, Boniface? By many years the record lied to me.
60: Art thou so early satiate with that wealth, For which thou didst not fear to take by fraud The beautiful Lady, and then work her woe?”
65: Such I became, as people are who stand, Not comprehending what is answered them, As if bemocked, and know not how to answer.
70: Then said Virgilius: “Say to him straightway, ‘I am not he, I am not he thou thinkest.’” And I replied as was imposed on me.
75: Whereat the spirit writhed with both his feet, Then, sighing, with a voice of lamentation Said to me: “Then what wantest thou of me?
80: If who I am thou carest so much to know, That thou on that account hast crossed the bank, Know that I vested was with the great mantle;
85: And truly was I son of the She-bear, So eager to advance the cubs, that wealth Above, and here myself, I pocketed.
90: Beneath my head the others are dragged down Who have preceded me in simony, Flattened along the fissure of the rock.
95: Below there I shall likewise fall, whenever That one shall come who I believed thou wast, What time the sudden question I proposed.
100: But longer I my feet already toast, And here have been in this way upside down, Than he will planted stay with reddened feet;
105: For after him shall come of fouler deed From tow’rds the west a Pastor without law, Such as befits to cover him and me.
110: New Jason will he be, of whom we read In Maccabees; and as his king was pliant, So he who governs France shall be to this one.”
116: I do not know if I were here too bold, That him I answered only in this metre: “I pray thee tell me now how great a treasure
121: Our Lord demanded of Saint Peter first, Before he put the keys into his keeping? Truly he nothing asked but ‘Follow me.’
126: Nor Peter nor the rest asked of Matthias Silver or gold, when he by lot was chosen Unto the place the guilty soul had lost.
131: Therefore stay here, for thou art justly punished, And keep safe guard o’er the ill-gotten money, Which caused thee to be valiant against Charles.
138: And were it not that still forbids it me The reverence for the keys superlative Thou hadst in keeping in the gladsome life,
139: I would make use of words more grievous still; Because your avarice afflicts the world, Trampling the good and lifting the depraved.
144: The Evangelist you Pastors had in mind, When she who sitteth upon many waters To fornicate with kings by him was seen;
145: The same who with the seven heads was born, And power and strength from the ten horns received, So long as virtue to her spouse was pleasing.
146: Ye have made yourselves a god of gold and silver; And from the idolater how differ ye, Save that he one, and ye a hundred worship?
150: Ah, Constantine! of how much ill was mother, Not thy conversion, but that marriage dower Which the first wealthy Father took from thee!”
152: And while I sang to him such notes as these, Either that anger or that conscience stung him, He struggled violently with both his feet.
153: I think in sooth that it my Leader pleased, With such contented lip he listened ever Unto the sound of the true words expressed.
154: Therefore with both his arms he took me up, And when he had me all upon his breast, Remounted by the way where he descended.
156: Nor did he tire to have me clasped to him; But bore me to the summit of the arch Which from the fourth dike to the fifth is passage.
162: There tenderly he laid his burden down, Tenderly on the crag uneven and steep, That would have been hard passage for the goats:
168: Thence was unveiled to me another valley.
174: Of a new pain behoves me to make verses And give material to the twentieth canto Of the first song, which is of the submerged.
180: I was already thoroughly disposed To peer down into the uncovered depth, Which bathed itself with tears of agony;
186: And people saw I through the circular valley, Silent and weeping, coming at the pace Which in this world the Litanies assume.
193: As lower down my sight descended on them, Wondrously each one seemed to be distorted From chin to the beginning of the chest;
196: For tow’rds the reins the countenance was turned, And backward it behoved them to advance, As to look forward had been taken from them.
